title: Can’t cite 2008 public hearing for Adani port’s 40% expansion proposal: Kattupalli fishers

read.desc: CHENNAI: Alleging that the proposed plan to expand Adani Kattupalli Port Pvt Ltd by 40 per cent, which would allow it to handle coal, petcoke, sulphur, and haza
paras: In a petition submitted ahead of an all department's recent review meeting chaired by the Tiruvallur district Collector at the Minjur Panchayat Union Office, the Kattupalli Kuppam Fishers Panchayat said the proposed expansion of the port's cargo handling capacity from 24.65 million metric tonnes per annum to 34.51 MMTPA would increase its capacity by 40%.

This expansion proposal by Marine Infrastructure Developer Private Limited (MIDPL) included handling dry bulk cargo such as coal, petcoke, iron ore, laterite stone, and sulphur, besides hazardous chemicals, the fishermen pointed out. They alleged that these cargo categories had never been presented to the public during the earlier public hearing conducted in August 2008.

The villagers also objected to MIDPL seeking exemption from a fresh public hearing by relying on the 2008 hearing and a Union Environment Ministry Office Memorandum dated April 11, 2022. They said the proposed expansion involved changes in the nature of cargo handled and an increase in pollution risks, making a fresh public hearing mandatory under environmental regulations.

The fishermen further warned that the proposed handling of hazardous chemicals could pose serious risks to nearby settlements. Citing the port's Environmental Impact Assessment report, they said a major damage of storage tanks could expose areas within 22 km to more than 50 km to toxic gas concentrations immediately dangerous to life.

The fishing community there urged the Tamil Nadu State Coastal Zone Management Authority to reject the port's request for exemption from a public hearing and not recommend coastal regulation zone clearance in its present form, and also demanded a fresh public hearing near the fishing village.

title: Adani Cement plans 410 electric trucks in india as freight economics shift

read.desc: Adani Cement targets 410 battery electric trucks by March 2027 amid shifting diesel and battery costs.
paras: Heavy road haulage has long been one of the hardest links in India's cement supply chain to decarbonise. Limestone, clinker and bagged cement require high-payload transport over demanding routes. Adani Cement is moving to shift a share of that workload onto electric power.

The company flagged off its initial electric haulage trucks at the Sanghi facility in Gujarat in mid-November 2026. These vehicles will move clinker and finished cement along active industrial corridors. Spanning brands such as Ambuja Cements, ACC and Orient Cement, the producer holds more than 113 million tonnes of annual installed capacity.

Management views the rollout as an early step toward electrifying 10% of its road logistics volume. That goal equates to over 2,000 electric trucks by 2030. The firm points to a structural tipping point in freight economics rather than a purely environmental gesture.

Higher diesel expenses, lower lithium-ion battery costs and falling solar tariffs are narrowing the operating gap for heavy electric trucks. Company estimates indicate that the 410-truck fleet could displace roughly 11 million litres of diesel each year. It could also cut carbon dioxide emissions by more than 25,000 tonnes annually when paired with renewable electricity.

Diesel trucks are calculated to emit about 0.7375 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilometre. Scaling electric heavy-duty freight across sprawling plant networks still tests charging availability, turnaround times and grid readiness along long-haul routes.

title: Adani to shut down 800MW unit from midnight

paras: Maintenance work to continue until 18 December; the power plant’s generation capacity will be halved during the period An 800-megawatt unit of Adani Power’s Godda power plant in India’s Jharkhand state will be shut down from midnight on Wednesday, 25 November, for annual maintenance. The unit is scheduled to remain out of operation until 18 December, while the plant’s other 800MW unit will continue generating electricity as usual, the Indian company said. In a statement sent to the media on Wednesday, Adani Power said the maintenance had been planned in advance as part of the plant’s routine maintenance programme. The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) approved the plan on 26 October. The work will include inspection and servicing of essential equipment, as well as measures to prevent potential technical faults in the future. The coal-fired Godda power plant has a total generation capacity of 1,600MW, with each of its two units capable of producing 800MW. However, under the power purchase agreement, the plant is required to supply a combined 1,496MW to Bangladesh. With one unit offline, the plant’s capacity to supply electricity to Bangladesh will be reduced by half during the maintenance period. In November 2017, the BPDB signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with Adani Power Jharkhand Limited. Under the deal, Adani built the Godda power plant at a cost of around $2 billion to supply electricity to Bangladesh. Power from its first unit began flowing into Bangladesh’s national grid on 9 March 2023. The maintenance shutdown comes as electricity demand in Bangladesh begins to decline with the onset of winter. According to data from the National Load Dispatch Centre (NLDC), electricity imports from India rose by around 37% in the first 15 days of November compared with the same period in October, despite a decline in domestic electricity demand and generation. Bangladesh imported an average of 33.6 million units of electricity a day during the first half of October. The daily average rose to 46 million units in the corresponding period of November. Mohammad Zahurul Islam, a BPDB member for generation, told bdnews24.com at the time that imports had increased because generating electricity from furnace oil was more expensive than importing power. Adani’s power supply to Bangladesh has previously been disrupted by technical faults and coal shortages. On 10 September, the plant’s second unit was shut down following a technical fault. It resumed generation three days later, on 13 September. NLDC data show that Adani supplied 1,430.06MW during the evening peak demand period on 9 September. After one unit was taken offline on 10 September, supply fell to 691.44MW.

title: Odisha: BJD opposes Adani data centre project, flags drinking water crisis risk

read.desc: Oppn alleges the Rs 1.4 lakh cr facility in Cuttack could strain drinking water resources in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, and Puri, and demands white paper on its viability and environmental impact
paras: Agencies 25 Nov 2026 7:00 PM IST (Updated: 2026-11-25 13:30:49 ) Bhubaneswar, Nov 25 (PTI) The opposition BJD on Wednesday strongly objected to the Odisha government's approval of a Rs 1.4 lakh crore data centre project in Cuttack, alleging that it could lead to water scarcity.

Raising the issue during Zero Hour in the assembly, Deputy Leader of Opposition Prasanna Acharya urged the government to reconsider its decision and clarify how the project would benefit the people of the state.

The proposed integrated data centre park by the Adani group, to be set up at Naraj on the banks of the Mahanadi in Cuttack district, will spread over around 250 acres and have a capacity of 1 gigawatt (GW). The project was approved by the High-Level Clearance Authority (HLCA), chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, in September 2025.
Acharya claimed the facility would require 2-4 crore units of electricity and around three crore litres of water every day, creating acute drinking water shortages in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Puri.

"We are not opposed to industries. But this particular project is dangerous for the state. This will create acute drinking water scarcity in the twin cities of Bhubaneswar and Cuttack besides causing problems for Puri district. I request the state government to reconsider its decision and scrap the project for the welfare of the people," he said.

read.desc: Navi Mumbai International Airport has crossed 4 million passengers and added nine domestic routes ahead of its Winter 2026 expansion.
paras: Navi Mumbai International Airport has handled 4,101,409 passengers since commercial operations began on December 25, 2025, according to a statement issued by the airport on November 25, ahead of its first anniversary.

The airport recorded 31,043 passenger aircraft movements and handled 40,868 metric tonnes of cargo up to November 15. Domestic travellers accounted for 4,088,840 passengers, while international passengers numbered 12,569. The airport recorded 2,023,241 arrivals and 2,078,168 departures during the period.

The figures position Navi Mumbai International Airport as a significant new aviation facility for the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, which now has a second international airport. The airport is developed and managed by Navi Mumbai International Airport Limited, a public-private partnership between Adani Airport Holdings Limited and the City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra.

Under its Winter 2026 schedule, the airport will serve 45 domestic and two international destinations. Nine domestic destinations have been added: Agatti via Goa’s Manohar International Airport, Bagdogra, Darbhanga, Guwahati, Jalgaon, Jodhpur, Ranchi, Sindhudurg and Udaipur.

Scheduled services to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia are due to begin on December 15. Jeddah will become the airport’s second international passenger destination after Abu Dhabi, where international passenger operations began in July 2026. The airport said the Jeddah route would serve business, leisure and religious pilgrimage travel.

read.desc: The dispute is over whether Indian drug laws apply to products sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs barrier, and whether nicotine pouches sold by Adani-backed retailers at Mumbai airport qualify as “drugs” under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act
paras: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Union government on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling which held that duty-free shops selling nicotine pouches at Mumbai airport cannot claim exemption from Indian regulatory laws.

A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi were hearing the challenge filed by Adani-backed retailer Mumbai Travel Retail Ltd and Flemingo Dutyfree Shop Pvt. Ltd, which operate duty-free outlets in the international departure area of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport.

The dispute is over whether Indian drug laws apply to products sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs barrier, and whether the nicotine pouches qualify as “drugs” under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

The high court in September rejected the retailers’ challenge to the regulatory action and held that goods sold at duty-free shops remain subject to Indian laws even if the shops are located beyond the customs barrier.

The dispute began after a 5 March 2026 inspection by a Ddrugs inspector at Terminal 2, where nicotine pouches sold under the FOX brand were found at a Mumbai Travel Retail outlet. The products included 3 mg and 6 mg nicotine pouches and, according to the court record, were imported from Sweden.

paras: Nagpur: Maharashtra’s power sector is heading for a major restructuring, with the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) set to replace 1,600 MW of electricity procurement from ageing Maharashtra State Power Generation Company Limited (MAHAGENCO) units with power from Adani Power at an approved tariff of ₹5.30 per unit.

The decision puts thermal power stations at Khaparkheda and Chandrapur in Vidarbha in focus, along with generating units at Bhusawal and Nashik. The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC), through its order dated June 19, 2026, approved MSEDCL’s proposal to procure 1,600 MW of coal-based thermal power from Adani Power.
The new arrangement is expected to begin in the financial year 2030–31 and will operate under a proposed 25-year Power Supply Agreement (PSA).

Under the proposal, MSEDCL has identified specific ageing and relatively expensive generating units whose existing power purchase agreements (PPAs) are proposed for early termination as replacement capacity becomes available.
Together, these units account for 1,600 MW of existing contracted capacity.

title: Maharashtra awards Adani company a contract to supply power using power from another Adani company

read.desc: The government overruled objections from competitors that the group’s company would have access to advantageous information.
paras: In March 2026, the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited, or MSEDCL, invited bids for the supply of 2,500 MW of electricity from companies willing to supply uninterrupted power, with a minimum of 51% drawn from traceable green energy.

On the surface, this appeared to be a routine tender. Uninterrupted, or round-the-clock, power packages are becoming increasingly popular in India because, rather than only focus on power generation, they ensure that end users receive a reliable electricity supply.
But documents accessed by Scroll reveal that several competing bidders raised concerns over a possible conflict of interest in the Maharashtra tender.

One of the companies in the fray was Adani Power. Other competing bidders objected to a clause in the tender that said that the winning bidder, as part of its round-the-clock supply package, would be bound to use solar power generated by another Adani-owned firm – Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five, which had an existing power-supply contract with MSEDCL.

In a pre-bid meeting that MSEDCL held with interested companies, one of the bidders stated: “We request not to allow the participation of any affiliate or Group company of M/s Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five Ltd… as it will create conflict of interest towards bidding in this tender and would provide an unfair advantage to their Affiliate and Group companies.”

title: Ambuja Cements firms up its next growth phase with ~30 MTPA expansion
snippet: The Company’s total capacity is expected to reach 119 MTPA by end of March 2027.

read.desc: Ambuja Cements firms up its next growth phase with ~30 MTPA expansion
paras: Ambuja Cements Limited, part of the Adani Portfolio and one of India's leading building materials solutions providers, has firmed up its next phase of expansion, with new greenfield and brownfield projects planned to add ~30 MTPA of cement capacity across key markets. The programme will expand its manufacturing network across the East, West, and North, building on its current 113.5 MTPA pan-India cement capacity across 24 integrated plants and 24 grinding units.

The expansion includes new grinding capacities of ~15.5 MTPA in West Cluster, 11.6 MTPA in East Cluster and 2.9 MTPA in North Cluster. Capacities added include at the East Cluster at Rangia (2.9 MTPA), Hojai (2.9 MTPA) in Assam; Godda (2.9 MTPA) in Jharkhand; Muzaffarpur (2.9 MTPA) in Bihar; West Cluster at Mundra (2.9 MTPA) and Hazira (2.9 MTPA) in Gujarat; Raigad (2.9 MTPA), Kalyan (2.9 MTPA), Dahanu (0.7 MTPA) and Amravati (2.9 MTPA) in Maharashtra; and North cluster at Dadri Line 2 (2.9 MTPA) in Uttar Pradesh. The programme also includes new clinker capacity in East cluster at Umrangso (4 MTPA) in Assam, West cluster at Maratha (4 MTPA) and Mundra (2.3 MTPA), strengthening the upstream network required to support the expanded grinding footprint.

Mr. Vinod Bahety, CEO Cement Business at Adani Group, said, “Our next phase of expansion is focused on quality of growth and creating a more balanced manufacturing network. By strengthening the link between clinker and grinding capacity and expanding closer to the high growth potential key markets, we are building greater flexibility into the network. As we scale, our focus is on combining market reach with logistics and cost efficiencies so that every capacity addition strengthens the competitiveness of the overall business. We have a vibrant supply chain ecosystem with stronger Brand Equity and share of Premium Cement in these markets. The growth footprint will compliment well with our value based strategic growth.

title: CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's rating to AA+/Stable

read.desc: CRISIL has upgraded Adani Power's credit rating to AA+/Stable from AA/Stable on bank loans and NCDs totalling ₹90,500 crore, the company said on Nov 24.
paras: Ahmedabad, November 24, 2026 CRISIL Limited has upgraded Adani Power Limited's credit rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Stable, the company told BSE and NSE on November 24, 2026, under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The rating covers enhanced bank loan and non-convertible debenture (NCD) facilities worth ₹90,500 crore in total.

And why did subsequent government assessments put the potential stamp duty shortfall at ₹249.63 crore? These are among the questions arising from the concession agreement for Lucknow's Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, involving the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited.

An investigation by New Delhi Post , based on official records obtained from the Uttar Pradesh Stamp Department, has uncovered a substantial discrepancy between the stamp duty paid when the agreement was executed and the liability subsequently assessed by government officials. The findings also bring the valuation of thousands of crores of rupees in airport land, the classification of the agreement and the treatment of public assets under scrutiny.

The concession agreement was signed on February 14, 2020, between the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited. It covered 1,258.80 acres of airport land and granted the private concessionaire rights relating to the airport's operation, management and development for 50 years.

Yet, the original e-stamp certificate classified the document under Article 5 – General Agreement. The property description was recorded as 'Not Applicable', the consideration was shown as zero, and the stamp duty paid was just ₹500.

This raises a fundamental question: how was an agreement involving long-term commercial rights over a major public infrastructure asset treated as a general agreement rather than a document attracting stamp duty based on the nature and value of the rights being granted?

title: Adani Enterprises incorporates wholly owned subsidiary Nashik Phata Road

read.desc: Adani Enterprises incorporates Nashik Phata Road Limited for an infrastructure project in Maharashtra.
paras: Adani Enterprises Limited has announced the incorporation of a new wholly owned subsidiary, Nashik Phata Road Limited (NPRL). The subsidiary was officially incorporated on 12th November 2026, with the certificate of incorporation received on 23rd November 2026, when the company was formally notified at 5:52 PM IST.

Nashik Phata Road Limited, formed under Indian jurisdiction, will focus on road infrastructure development. NPRL's primary project involves the development, maintenance, and management of an ambitious road infrastructure initiative involving an 8-lane elevated flyover. This project spans the Nashik Phata to Khed section (Km 12.190 to KM 42.113) of National Highway (NH)-60 in Maharashtra, utilising the BOT (Build, Operate, Transfer) Toll model.

According to the details outlined in the regulatory disclosure filed by Adani Enterprises, Nashik Phata Road Limited has been established with an authorised and paid-up capital of Rs. 1,00,000, structured as 10,000 equity shares each priced at Rs. 10. Adani Enterprises holds 100% of the shareholding in NPRL, reaffirming its direct involvement and control over the subsidiary.

There are no government or regulatory queries affecting the incorporation status of the subsidiary. The creation of Nashik Phata Road Limited aligns with Adani Enterprises' strategic focus on expanding its footprint in infrastructure and development projects across India.

The establishment of NPRL marks a significant step in Adani Enterprises' continued growth within the infrastructure sector, particularly in enhancing roadway infrastructure in the state of Maharashtra.

paras: Mumbai: Diamond Power Infrastructure Ltd’s new data centre cable business generated ₹ 242 crore in revenue in its first month of operations, accounting for a fourth of its July-September revenue. The early traction marks a significant step in the company’s efforts to diversify beyond the Adani Group, which has dominated its order book.

The company began supplying cables from its newly commissioned copper cable line in September, just a month after raising ₹ 1,614 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), its management said during its 4 November earnings call. Its copper cable manufacturing capacity currently stands at 1,500 tonnes a month, which it plans to increase to 2,500 tonnes.

"The QIP funds came into the company in August. In September, the very next month, we achieved record production of ₹ 575 crores. Of that, our team made and delivered ₹ 242 crores of data centre cables in a single month," Amit Bhatnagar, head of corporate strategy at Diamond Power, told analysts in its 4 November earnings call.

The cables were delivered to data centre engineering, procurement, and construction contractors like L&T , AurionPro, Sterling and Wilson, and Blue Star, he said. The new business helped the Gujarat-based cable and conductor manufacturer more than double its quarterly revenue year-on-year to ₹ 1,032 crore.

The quick start comes as companies in the data centre supply chain are banking on a growing opportunity as India builds more facilities to meet demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence. Around 3,860 megawatts (MW) of new data centre capacity is planned or under construction through 2030, according to a September report by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield.

title: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani's scrapped Kenya power deal carries $339 million exit bill

paras: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani's cancelled power-line deal in Kenya could cost the country Sh43.94 billion ($339 million) to unwind, two years after President William Ruto ordered it scrapped.

The estimate appears in the National Treasury's fifth annual report on the state of public-private partnerships in Kenya, covering the year to June 2026. It is the termination payment linked to the contract between Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. and the state-owned Kenya Electricity Transmission Co., known as Ketraco.
The report describes the sum as a contingent liability rather than an amount due immediately. It does not break the figure down or disclose the costs Adani has submitted for verification.

Adani Energy Solutions signed the 30-year deal with Ketraco in October 2024 to build, finance and run power lines and substations. The wider agreement was valued at Sh95.68 billion ($739 million). The two lines named in the termination estimate, the 400-kilovolt Lessos-Loosuk line and the 220-kilovolt Kisumu (Kibos)-Kakamega-Musaga line, were expected to cost about Sh41 billion ($317 million) together.
That puts the estimated exit payment about Sh3 billion above the cost of building the two lines.

title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks

read.desc: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the
paras: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the first batch as part of the initiative and will commission the remaining trucks by March 2027.

Based on images shared with the announcement, Adani Cement appears to have procured eleven units initially. The company has deployed these heavy-duty electric trucks at its Sanghi plant in the western state of Gujarat and is using them to transport clinker and cement. It says the movement of both these materials is a carbon-intensive part of the cement industry’s operations.

The first batch comprises Chinese manufacturer Sany’s 55-tonne heavy-duty electric trucks. These units appear to be either the 5538E or the 5550E, the two 55-tonne high-roof models the company offers in India, both of which have a 4×2 drivetrain layout and pack 360 kW of power. The 5538E uses a 282 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 240 kW and delivers a range of 189 km. The 5550E upgrades to a 376 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 360 kW and increases the range to 245 km.

Adani Cement says the economics are now in favour of electric trucks in India’s cement industry. The company says that while diesel prices have increased by 60 per cent over the past decade, lithium-ion battery pack costs and solar tariffs have fallen by approximately 70 per cent and 47 per cent, respectively. It also states that diesel trucks emit approximately 737.5 grams of CO2 per kilometre. The company estimates its 410 electric trucks will reduce its diesel consumption by 11 million litres per year and avoid more than 25,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually.

Vinod Bahety, CEO of the Cement Business at Adani Group, said the company has identified multiple routes across the country for transporting clinker and cement using electric trucks. Its plan to deploy 410 electric trucks by March 2027 represents the first phase of electrifying these transport operations. By 2030, the company aims to expand its fleet to over 2,000 electric trucks and use them to handle 10 per cent of its road freight.

title: CERC Allows CSPDCL to Amend Adani Solar Safeguard Duty Claim

read.desc: CERC permits Chhattisgarh Discom to amend its ₹85.28 crore safeguard duty claim against Adani Solar under Change in Law provisions.
paras: The regulatory landscape governing India’s renewable energy sector often encounters disputes revolving around ‘Change in Law’ events. In a recent development, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued an order allowing the Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Co. Ltd. (CSPDCL) to amend its petition involving a substantial ₹85.28 crore safeguard duty claim against Adani Solar Energy Jaisalmer One Pvt. Ltd. The core of the dispute traces back to the imposition and subsequent removal of safeguard duty (SGD) on imported solar cells, a fiscal element that directly impacts project economics and power purchase agreement (PPA) tariffs.

CSPDCL procures power from Adani Solar’s 450 MW solar project located in Rajasthan through an intermediary agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI). The state distribution company contends that the expiration and removal of the 15% safeguard duty effective from 30 July 2021 constitutes a ‘Change in Law’ event under the PPA terms. According to CSPDCL, this regulatory shift reduced Adani Solar’s operational costs, and the resulting financial benefit should rightfully be passed on to the consumers in Chhattisgarh through a lower tariff or a direct refund of ₹85.28 crore along with applicable interest.

During the proceedings, CSPDCL sought to amend its petition to include a government notification dated 30 July 2018, correcting references that previously only highlighted a later notification from 29 July 2020. Adani Solar strongly opposed the amendment, arguing that the request was time-barred beyond the three-year limitation period, relied on assumptions rather than actual costs, and that the expiry of the 2018 notification was anticipated. However, CERC dismissed Adani’s objections as hyper-technical, classifying the amendment as a clarification rather than a novel case that prejudices the developer, while noting that Adani remains free to contest the substantive merits during the main hearings.

title: Adani Energy Solutions Secures Rs 500 Cr Bihar Transmission Project

read.desc: Adani Energy Solutions wins a Bihar transmission project linked to a 2,400 MW thermal plant, with annual tariff revenue of Rs 500 crore.
paras: Adani Energy Solutions has expanded its presence in India’s transmission sector after securing a Bihar project linked to the evacuation of power from a 2,400 MW thermal plant. The asset is expected to generate about Rs 500 crore in annual tariff revenue. The project falls under India’s tariff-based competitive bidding framework and will establish the transmission network for the Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant in Bihar. The transmission system has a completion target of the fourth quarter of 2028.

The award adds another regulated transmission asset to Adani Energy Solutions’ portfolio as India steps up investment in power networks to accommodate new generation capacity and rising electricity consumption.

Asset Base Expands The Bihar project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 megavolt-ampere (MVA) of transformation capacity to the company’s network. The company’s transmission portfolio will reach 30,683 ckm of lines and 146,585 MVA of transformation capacity after the addition. Its cumulative transmission capital expenditure will also rise to about Rs 91,500 crore. Vikramshila Power Transmission, a special purpose vehicle created for the transmission scheme, will implement the project.

Network Links Generation The transmission system will connect the Pirpainti generation complex with key nodes in Bihar’s power network. The scope covers new substations and high-voltage transmission corridors that will carry electricity from the upcoming thermal generation facility.

The scheme includes four gas-insulated substations (GIS) and transmission links at the 400 kV and 220 kV levels. The network will connect Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, while additional links will strengthen connectivity with Bakhtiyarpur and other parts of the state’s transmission system.
